Project Style Guide

Source: project-style-guide.md

R package + interactive HTML report + multi-tier distribution

David Gomez-Zepeda — for use as context in new similar projects

Project architecture pattern

This style of project follows a layered architecture:

LC-MS processed data (e.g., PEAKS CSV export, Fragpipe .tsv, DIA-NN .txt or p.parquet)
      │
      ▼
R functions   — normalise, annotate, threshold, summarise
      │
      ▼
Parameterised RMarkdown template (inst/rmarkdown/templates/)
      — produces a self-contained, interactive HTML report
      — all parameters declared in YAML header under params:
      — toggle static/interactive plots via params$PlotsInteractive
      │
      ▼
Multiple csv files — incl. always-written input_params.csv (version + all params)
Excel workbook   — summary tables via write.xlsx()

Distribution tiers (always provide all four, ordered easiest → most powerful):

Tier Mechanism Audience
1 Windows .bat launcher Anyone, no coding, Windows
2 Shiny browser app via Docker Anyone, no coding, any OS
3 Docker CLI Intermediate, scripting/batch
4 R package Advanced, full programmatic access

R package conventions

DESCRIPTION

  • Use specific sub-packages, not meta-packages (dplyr, tidyr, forcats — not tidyverse)
  • Imports vs Suggests split: packages used via :: in R/ files → Imports; packages only used inside the Rmd template → Suggests. Do not move Rmd-only packages into Imports (triggers “Namespaces in Imports not imported from” CI warning).
  • Common Suggests for this pattern: DT, openxlsx, plotly, scales, shiny, bslib
  • Common Imports: dplyr, tidyr, forcats, ggplot2, rmarkdown, knitr
  • knitr goes in Imports (not Suggests) if used via knitr:: in any R/ file
  • Bump version in both DESCRIPTION and CLAUDE.md when releasing

NAMESPACE and man/ — never edit by hand

NAMESPACE and all man/*.Rd files are generated by roxygen2. The correct workflow: 1. Fix @param tags in the R/ source file 2. Run devtools::document() to regenerate 3. After running, always check git status man/ — if fewer files changed than expected, run devtools::document() again 4. Only commit once every relevant Rd file is regenerated

roxygen2 rules

  • Every @examples block must be wrapped in \dontrun{} — no exceptions, even for pure functions. R CMD CHECK runs unwrapped examples and the package has no real instrument data in the check environment.
  • @param tags must exactly match the function signature. Mismatches cause Rd \usage sections CI warnings (treated as errors).
  • Add @keywords internal to suppress export from the pkgdown site without removing the export.
  • Every new exported function must be added to _pkgdown.yml reference section in the same PR, or the pkgdown Action fails with "topic missing from index: 'XYZ'".

Coding patterns

  • %>% pipe is re-exported by dplyr — no need to import separately
  • No require() calls inside functions — all dependencies declared in DESCRIPTION and imported via @import in a package-level file (e.g., R/help.R)
  • Use ... (dot-dot-dot) for flexible grouping arguments in summary functions — makes them reusable across different aggregation levels without code duplication
  • RiskLevel and similar ordered factors: always use integer codes for computation/colour-scaling, labels for display; define the mapping as a named constant
  • replace_na(col, replace = 0) on a column that could be all-NA: wrap with as.numeric() first — otherwise R infers the column as NA_logical_ and replace_na returns FALSE instead of 0
  • replicate(n, expr, simplify = FALSE) — first arg is count, second is expression (easy to swap)
  • When replacing a deeply nested call with a simpler helper, recount closing parens — the nesting depth changes

Tests (testthat edition 3)

  • Tests live in tests/testthat/
  • For functions that check file.exists("relative/path"): use setwd(tmpdir) + on.exit(setwd(old_wd)) so the relative-path check hits the test-controlled directory, not the real CWD
  • CI must pass with 0 errors, 0 warnings on both Windows and Ubuntu before merging to main

Shiny app conventions

  • UI: bslib::page_sidebar() layout
  • Theme: bs_theme(primary = <brand_colour>, secondary = <accent_colour>) matched to the package logo palette
  • Logo: place in inst/shiny/www/ — Shiny serves this directory as static assets automatically
  • File output: always use downloadHandler() + downloadButton(). Never add a text input for a user-chosen output path — browsers cannot let a web server write to a user-selected local path (security constraint)
  • The Shiny app is distributed as a separate Docker image (:app tag) extending the CLI image (:latest)
  • shiny and bslib in Suggests, not Imports

Shiny Docker image tag — critical

GHCR requires all-lowercase image names. ${{ github.repository_owner }} in GitHub Actions preserves mixed-case (e.g., DavidGZ1). Always hardcode the lowercase tag in the workflow:

tags: ghcr.io/davidgz1/mypackage:app   # correct
tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/mypackage:app  # WRONG — will fail

Docker conventions

Base image and build

  • Base: rocker/r-ver:4.2.0 (or appropriate version)
  • Use renv::restore() from renv.lock for reproducible dependency installs
  • Three system-level requirements to add to apt-get on Ubuntu Focal:
    • cmake — required by nloptr
    • libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev — required by textshaping/ragg
    • pandoc — not included in rocker/r-ver (unlike rocker/tidyverse); required for rmarkdown render
  • Matrix version conflict: if renv.lock pins Matrix 1.4-1 but MatrixModels >= 1.4-2 is needed, bump Matrix to 1.5-4.1 in renv.lock and drop the Hash field (renv recomputes it). Do not try to pre-install Matrix and use exclude= — renv’s sandboxed lib.loc doesn’t see the site-library.

CLI entrypoint pattern

  • docker/entrypoint.sh — bash script parsing --flag value args
  • docker/run_report.R — called by entrypoint, invokes the main report function
  • Expose all report parameters as CLI flags; document them in README with a table

Windows usage gotchas

  • Docker CLI not on PATH by default after Docker Desktop install. README and .bat launcher must address this.
  • Volume mount maps a Windows path to a container path: -v "C:\host\folder:/data". All file arguments must use the container-side path (/data/file.csv), not the Windows path.

Windows .bat launcher rules

  • Never put a :label inside a parenthesised if (...) or for (...) block — cmd.exe silently terminates the block at the label, causing unpredictable early exit. All labels must be at top scope; use goto to jump to them.
  • All error paths must converge at a :error_exit label that always calls pause before exit /b 1 — this keeps the window open so the user can read the error.
  • Suppress Docker output with >nul 2>&1 for daemon checks; show docker pull output so the user sees progress.
  • Use timeout /t N /nobreak >nul for silent waits; never use sleep.
  • Test with a double-click from Windows Explorer (not from a terminal) — the PATH and CWD may differ.

Branch and release strategy

  • main — stable releases only
  • dev — integration branch; all work lands here first, then merges to main
  • CI: R CMD CHECK on Windows + Ubuntu on every push/PR to both branches
  • Merging to main triggers Docker image builds and pkgdown site deployment
  • Version bumps: update DESCRIPTION (Version field) and CLAUDE.md (current version line) together
  • GitHub Releases: tag as vX.Y.Z, attach the .bat launcher as a release asset so non-technical users have a direct download link
  • The releases/latest URL in README always resolves to the newest release asset

pkgdown site

  • Configured in _pkgdown.yml, deployed to GitHub Pages on push to main
  • Every exported topic must appear in the reference: section — including the package-level help page (man/PackageName.Rd)
  • To exclude a topic from the site: add @keywords internal to its roxygen block
